claim: The overactivation of NF-κB signaling is a key hallmark for the pathogenesis of extranodal natural killer/T cell lymphoma (ENKTL).
source: The overactivation of NF-κB signaling is a key hallmark for the pathogenesis of extranodal natural killer/T cell lymphoma (ENKTL), a very aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma yet with rather limited control strategies.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Wen et al., 2018) as stated in the Introduction section.

claim: ENKTL is a very aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with rather limited control strategies.
source: The overactivation of NF-κB signaling is a key hallmark for the pathogenesis of extranodal natural killer/T cell lymphoma (ENKTL), a very aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma yet with rather limited control strategies.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Yamaguchi et al., 2018) and established knowledge about ENKTL.

claim: ENKTL has rather poor prognosis and short median survival time.
source: ENKTL represents as a rare yet highly aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) (Yamaguchi et al., 2018) with rather poor prognosis and short median survival time (Suzuki et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Suzuki et al., 2010.

claim: The dysregulated exportin-1 (CRM1) is mainly responsible for tumor cells to evade apoptosis and promote tumor-associated pathways such as NF-κB signaling.
source: Previously, we found that the dysregulated exportin-1 (also known as CRM1) is mainly responsible for tumor cells to evade apoptosis and promote tumor-associated pathways such as NF-κB signaling.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' previous findings as stated in the Abstract.

claim: Targeted therapy towards ENKTL is still lacking.
source: Nevertheless, to date, targeted therapy towards ENKTL is still lacking and new therapeutic strategies are urgently needed to combat this rare yet deadly tumor (Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2015.

claim: CRM1 has been implicated in the aggressive behavior of various malignancies by nuclear exporting critical tumor suppressor proteins and transcription factors.
source: Exportin-1, also known as CRM1, has been implicated in the aggressive behavior of various malignances by nuclear exporting critical tumor suppressor proteins and transcription factors (Dong et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dong et al., 2009.

claim: CRM1 has been found to be highly upregulated in a panel of tumor types.
source: Moreover, CRM1 has been found to be highly upregulated in a panel of tumor types (Turner et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Turner et al., 2012.

claim: Tumor cells strive to evade powerful negative regulation of apoptosis and cell proliferation through CRM1-mediated nuclear export machinery.
source: Indeed, it is believed that tumor cells strive to evade powerful negative regulation of apoptosis and cell proliferation through CRM1-mediated nuclear export machinery.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in the field as indicated by 'it is believed'.

claim: Sulforaphene and its synthetic analogues can selectively kill a panel of tumor cells.
source: Previously, we reported that a natural and covalent CRM1 inhibitor sulforaphene and its synthetic analogues (Wang et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2023; Gao et al., 2021), can selectively kill a panel of tumor cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: A deep reinforcement learning molecular de novo design model was used to facilitate the discovery of novel aromatic fragments for CRM1 inhibitors.
source: Briefly, we adopted the deep reinforcement learning molecular de novo design model developed by Olivecrona et al., 2017 to facilitate the discovery of novel aromatic fragments.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Olivecrona et al., 2017 and describes the methodology used.

claim: The deep reinforcement learning model prioritizes structures with modest similarity to molecules in the positive dataset of known CRM1 inhibitors rather than very close analogues.
source: This model prioritizes those structures with modest similarity to the molecules in the positive dataset of known CRM1 inhibitors rather than very close analogues.
evidence: This claim describes the design principle of the computational model used.

claim: An initial output of 3,000 moiety structures was obtained from the deep reinforcement learning model.
source: We obtained an initial output of 3,000 moiety structures and the top 50 candidate moieties generated from this step were used as seed structures to search for commercial-available aromatic fragments from Sigma-Aldrich compound library (similarity ~97%).
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental data from the computational screening.

claim: Ten commercial-accessible aromatic fragments were selected and purchased for experimental testing via biolayer interferometry assay (BLI).
source: Next, we selected and purchased 10 commercial-accessible aromatic fragments (Figure 1A) which were experimentally tested via biolayer interferometry assay (BLI).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental methodology described and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Tetrazole moieties (S5 and S8 fragment) obtained the second highest binding constant with CRM1 via BLI assay experiments.
source: Among the ten experimentally tested fragments, tetrazole moieties (S5 and S8 fragment) obtained the second highest binding constant with CRM1 via BLI assay experiments (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tetrazole fragments are more synthetically accessible compared to the fragment with the highest binding constant (S4 moiety).
source: Yet, given that tetrazole fragments are more synthetic accessible as compared to the fragment with the highest binding constant (S4 moiety in Figure 1A, benzo[d]oxazol-2-yl)-N, N-dimethylaniline), the tetrazole moiety was chosen to install with sulforaphene parent structure.
evidence: This claim is based on inference about synthetic accessibility considerations.

claim: LFS-1107 binds strongly with CRM1 with a Kd of approximately 1.25E-11 M.
source: Our BLI results revealed that LFS-1107 binds strongly with CRM1 (Kd~1.25E-11 M, Figure 1D) as compared to KPT-330 (Kd~5.29E-09 M), a known CRM1 inhibitor approved by FDA.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental BLI data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: KPT-330 binds to CRM1 with a Kd of approximately 5.29E-09 M.
source: Our BLI results revealed that LFS-1107 binds strongly with CRM1 (Kd~1.25E-11 M, Figure 1D) as compared to KPT-330 (Kd~5.29E-09 M), a known CRM1 inhibitor approved by FDA.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental BLI data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: KPT-330 is a known CRM1 inhibitor approved by FDA.
source: Our BLI results revealed that LFS-1107 binds strongly with CRM1 (Kd~1.25E-11 M, Figure 1D) as compared to KPT-330 (Kd~5.29E-09 M), a known CRM1 inhibitor approved by FDA.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about KPT-330.

claim: LFS-1107 doesn't bind with IkBα or Keap1 in BLI assay experiments.
source: In contrast, LFS-1107 doesn't bind with either two control probes IkBα or Keap1 in BLI assay experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental BLI data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: LFS-1107 is a reversible CRM1 inhibitor with clear dissociation process.
source: Furthermore, the results revealed that LFS-1107 is a reversible CRM1 inhibitor with clear dissociation process which may implicate a low toxicity profile.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental BLI data showing dissociation kinetics.

claim: Sulforaphene synthetic analogues are reversible CRM1 inhibitors.
source: This is consistent with the results of our previous studies that sulforaphene synthetic analogues are reversible CRM1 inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The GSH:GSSG ratio keeps constant upon the treatment of LFS-1107.
source: Moreover, we used GSH/GSSG detection assay kit to show that the GSH:GSSG ratio keeps constant upon the treatment of LFS-1107 and therefore we ruled out the possibility that LFS-1107 is a general redox modulator (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: LFS-1107 is not a general redox modulator.
source: Moreover, we used GSH/GSSG detection assay kit to show that the GSH:GSSG ratio keeps constant upon the treatment of LFS-1107 and therefore we ruled out the possibility that LFS-1107 is a general redox modulator (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the GSH/GSSG ratio data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CRM1 is a major cellular target of LFS-1107 and responsible for its cellular activities.
source: Collectively, our results revealed that CRM1 is a major cellular target of LFS-1107 and responsible for its cellular activities.
evidence: This claim is based on multiple experimental results including BLI assays and siRNA knockdown experiments.

claim: LFS-1107 achieves IC50 value of 26 nM in SNK6 cell line.
source: Our data show that LFS-1107 achieves IC50 value of 26 nM in SNK6 cell line and 36 nM in HANK-1 cell line (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental cell viability data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: LFS-1107 achieves IC50 value of 36 nM in HANK-1 cell line.
source: Our data show that LFS-1107 achieves IC50 value of 26 nM in SNK6 cell line and 36 nM in HANK-1 cell line (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental cell viability data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: LFS-1107 barely showed any toxicity at concentration of 4 μM in normal PBMCs.
source: Interestingly, LFS-1107 barely showed any toxicity at concentration of 4 μM and the toxicity towards normal human PBMC is minimal even at a high dose of 9 μM.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental cytotoxicity data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The toxicity of LFS-1107 towards normal human PBMC is minimal even at a high dose of 9 μM.
source: Interestingly, LFS-1107 barely showed any toxicity at concentration of 4 μM and the toxicity towards normal human PBMC is minimal even at a high dose of 9 μM.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental cytotoxicity data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: LFS-1107 can selectively eliminate ENKTL cells while sparing normal human PBMC with good safety profile.
source: This implicates that LFS-1107 can selectively eliminate ENKTL cells while sparing normal human PBMC with good safety profile.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential toxicity data between ENKTL cells and normal PBMCs.

claim: LFS-1107 barely exhibits any effects on human platelets even at very high concentrations of 500 μM.
source: We assessed the toxicity effects of LFS-1107 towards platelets and we found that LFS-1107 barely exhibits any effects on human platelets even at very high concentrations of 500 μM (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental platelet viability data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: LFS-1107 could suppress the expression of CRM1 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: First, we demonstrated that LFS-1107 could suppress the expression of CRM1 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The cellular activities by LFS-1107 was significantly abrogated when CRM1 was knocked down by siCRM1.
source: We revealed that the cellular activities by LFS-1107 was significantly abrogated when CRM1 was knocked down by siCRM1, implicating that CRM1 is a main target responsible for the cellular activities of LFS-1107 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: LFS-1107 can lead to nuclear accumulation of IκBα after 3 hr treatment in a dose dependent manner.
source: Our immunofluorescent results by confocal microscopy revealed that LFS-1107 can lead to nuclear accumulation of IκBα after 3 hr treatment in a dose dependent manner (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: IκBα was trapped in the nucleus as the protein level of nuclear IκBα was significantly upregulated after LFS-1107 treatment.
source: The results ascertained that IκBα was trapped in the nucleus as the protein level of nuclear IκBα was significantly upregulated after LFS-1107 treatment (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data of nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The expression of proinflammatory and proliferative proteins p65, COX-2, c-Myc, and Survivin were downregulated in a dose dependent manner after treatment with LFS-1107.
source: Consequently, we found the expression of proinflammatory and proliferative proteins p65, COX-2, c-Myc, and Survivin were downregulated in a dose dependent manner after treatment with LFS-1107 (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Treatment of SNK6 cells with LFS-1107 resulted in a significant reduction of proinflammatory cytokines including TNF-α, IFN-γ, NF-κB/p65, IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and MCP-1.
source: Furthermore, when SNK6 cells were treated with LFS-1107, we observed a significant reduction of the proinflammatory cytokines including TNF-α, IFN-γ, NF-κB/p65, IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and MCP-1 as measured by ELISA assay (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2K.

claim: Biological Process (regulation of cellular component organization) and Molecular Function (protein binding) related to CRM1 were modulated upon the treatment of LFS-1107.
source: Moreover, proteomics analysis suggests that Biological Process (regulation of cellular component organization) and Molecular Function (protein binding) related to CRM1 were modulated upon the treatment of LFS-1107 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomics and Gene Ontology analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The inhibition of CRM1 by LFS-1107 could lead to the downregulation of NF-κB transcriptional activity, proinflammatory cytokines and oncogenic signatures of ENKTL.
source: These results suggested that the inhibition of CRM1 by LFS-1107 could lead to the downregulation of NF-κB transcriptional activity, proinflammatory cytokines and oncogenic signatures of ENKTL.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from multiple experimental results including Western blots, ELISA, and proteomics data.

claim: LFS-1107 treatment (10 mg/kg/week) was able to extend mouse survival in a xenograft mouse model.
source: We found that LFS-1107 treatment (10 mg/kg/week) was able to extend mouse survival (Figure 3A–B) and eliminate tumor cells considerably as evidenced by flow cytometric analysis (Figure 3C–D–E), demonstrating the efficacy of LFS-1107 in controlling ENKTL.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo survival data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: LFS-1107 treatment eliminated tumor cells considerably as evidenced by flow cytometric analysis.
source: We found that LFS-1107 treatment (10 mg/kg/week) was able to extend mouse survival (Figure 3A–B) and eliminate tumor cells considerably as evidenced by flow cytometric analysis (Figure 3C–D–E), demonstrating the efficacy of LFS-1107 in controlling ENKTL.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C-D-E.

claim: Mice injected with LFS-1107 reduced splenomegaly and restored spleen weight and spleen volume as compared with the normal group.
source: Moreover, remarkably, mice injected with LFS-1107 reduced splenomegaly and restored spleen weight and spleen volume as compared with the normal group (Figure 3F–G) with a better overall survival rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by spleen weight and volume data shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: Splenomegaly is a conventional symptom for extranodal natural NK/T cell lymphoma patients.
source: Noteworthy, splenomegaly is a conventional symptom for extranodal natural NK/T cell lymphoma patients (Tse and Kwong, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tse and Kwong, 2017.

claim: LFS-1107 can ameliorate the symptoms of ENKTL.
source: Hence, our results implicate that LFS-1107 can ameliorate the symptoms of ENKTL and might be a potentially promising compound for ENKTL treatment.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the in vivo data showing reduction in splenomegaly and improved survival.

claim: LFS-1107 might be a potentially promising compound for ENKTL treatment.
source: Hence, our results implicate that LFS-1107 can ameliorate the symptoms of ENKTL and might be a potentially promising compound for ENKTL treatment.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the cumulative experimental evidence presented.

claim: Treatment of LFS-1107 holds great promise as an effective remedy for ENKTL, acting through the nuclear retention of IkBα and subsequent attenuation of NF-κB signaling.
source: In summary, we report the discovery and biological evaluation of a synthetic sulforaphene analogue as potent CRM1 inhibitor towards the treatment of ENKTL. We demonstrated that treatment of LFS-1107 holds great promise as an effective remedy for ENKTL, acting through the nuclear retention of IkBα and subsequent attenuation of NF-κB signaling.
evidence: This claim is based on the cumulative experimental evidence from cell-based and in vivo studies.

claim: LFS-1107 may kill ENKTL cells via other mechanisms due to the broad-spectrum cargo proteins of CRM1.
source: We want to remind the reader that we don't rule out the possibility that LFS-1107 may kill ENKTL cells via other mechanisms due to the broad-spectrum cargo proteins of CRM1.
evidence: This claim is speculative and acknowledges potential alternative mechanisms.

claim: The study has captured the most prominent mechanism of actions for LFS-1107 towards ENKTL.
source: Yet, we want to argue that our study has captured the most prominent mechanism of actions for LFS-1107 towards ENKTL.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the comprehensive experimental data presented.

claim: The study represents a novel route for eliminating ENKTL tumor cells with a distinct mode of actions.
source: Our study may represent a novel route for eliminating ENKTL tumor cells with a distinct mode of actions.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the overall findings and their novelty.

claim: LFS-1107 holds great promise for the treatment of ENKTL and may warrant translation for use in clinical trials.
source: Therefore, LFS-1107 holds great promise for the treatment of ENKTL and may warrant translation for use in clinical trials.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the preclinical data presented.

claim: CRM1 was significantly elevated in patients with Lymphoma.
source: It shows that CRM1 was significantly elevated in patients with Lymphoma.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: LFS-1107 can strongly suppress the growth of ENKTL cells at low-range nanomolar concentration.
source: We found that LFS-1107 can strongly suppresses the growth of ENKTL cells at low-range nanomolar concentration yet with minimal effects on human platelets and healthy peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability data showing IC50 values in the nanomolar range.

claim: LFS-1107 has minimal effects on human platelets and healthy peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
source: We found that LFS-1107 can strongly suppresses the growth of ENKTL cells at low-range nanomolar concentration yet with minimal effects on human platelets and healthy peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by cytotoxicity data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in the nuclear retention of IkBα.
source: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in the nuclear retention of IkBα and consequent strong suppression of NF-κB transcriptional activities, NF-κB target genes downregulation and attenuated tumor cell growth and proliferation.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figures 2G-H and 2J.

claim: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in strong suppression of NF-κB transcriptional activities.
source: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in the nuclear retention of IkBα and consequent strong suppression of NF-κB transcriptional activities, NF-κB target genes downregulation and attenuated tumor cell growth and proliferation.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and ELISA data showing downregulation of NF-κB target genes and cytokines.

claim: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in NF-κB target genes downregulation.
source: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in the nuclear retention of IkBα and consequent strong suppression of NF-κB transcriptional activities, NF-κB target genes downregulation and attenuated tumor cell growth and proliferation.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data showing downregulation of p65, COX-2, c-Myc, and Survivin.

claim: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in attenuated tumor cell growth and proliferation.
source: Treatment of ENKTL cells with LFS-1107 resulted in the nuclear retention of IkBα and consequent strong suppression of NF-κB transcriptional activities, NF-κB target genes downregulation and attenuated tumor cell growth and proliferation.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assays and in vivo tumor burden data.

claim: LFS-1107 exhibited potent activities when administered to immunodeficient mice engrafted with human ENKTL cells.
source: Furthermore, LFS-1107 exhibited potent activities when administered to immunodeficient mice engrafted with human ENKTL cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The overactivation of NF-κB signaling and its downstream cytokines is a key hallmark for the pathogenesis of ENKTL.
source: Previously, we and colleagues uncovered that the overactivation of NF-κB signaling and its downstream cytokines is a key hallmark for the pathogenesis of ENKTL (Wen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wen et al., 2018.

claim: The reversible nature of LFS-1107 binding to CRM1 may implicate a low toxicity profile.
source: Furthermore, the results revealed that LFS-1107 is a reversible CRM1 inhibitor with clear dissociation process which may implicate a low toxicity profile.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on inference from the reversible binding kinetics.

claim: Nuclear accumulation of IκBα induced by LFS-1107 treatment is reversible upon washing.
source: Nuclear accumulation of IκBα induced by treatment with LFS-1107 (500nM) for 3 hours. The medium (containing LFS-1107) was removed and replaced with new medium in the Wash group.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 showing reversibility of nuclear accumulation.

claim: The deep reinforcement learning model was pre-trained with about 2 million structures from the PubChem database.
source: The Design module was first pre-trained with about ~2 million structures from the PubChem database to learn basic rules of organic chemistry that define SMILES strings within the context of Recurrent neural network (RNN).
evidence: This claim describes the training methodology for the computational model.

claim: 97% of the generated structures from the deep reinforcement learning model were chemically sensible structures.
source: To check the validity of the approach, we used the module to generate about 0.2 million compounds which were assessed by the structure checker ChemAxon and 97% of the generated structures were chemical sensible structures.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational validation data.

claim: The model prioritizes the synthetic feasibility of a small-molecule compound.
source: The model prioritizes the synthetic feasibility of a small-molecule compound, and the distinctiveness of the compound from other molecules in the literatures and in the patent space.
evidence: This claim describes the design principles of the computational model.

claim: The model prioritizes the distinctiveness of the compound from other molecules in the literatures and in the patent space.
source: The model prioritizes the synthetic feasibility of a small-molecule compound, and the distinctiveness of the compound from other molecules in the literatures and in the patent space.
evidence: This claim describes the design principles of the computational model.

claim: IkBα and Keap1 are reactive for covalent compounds and frequently used for testing selectivity.
source: Here, we chose IkBα and Keap1 as two control probes to compare because both of them are reactive for covalent compounds and thereby frequently used for testing selectivity.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in the field of covalent inhibitor development.

claim: Drug-induced toxicity towards platelets (thrombocytopenia) is a common side effect in clinical trials for cancer therapeutics.
source: Moreover, drug-induced toxicity towards platelets (also called as thrombocytopenia) is a common side effect in clinical trials for cancer therapeutics.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in clinical oncology.
